cards.body:
## Summary
Make the schema a caller already declares the one enforced contract for every text and vision provider: the engine parses once, validates once, and throws a typed EngineError instead of handing back a string cast as T. Providers sit behind one registry, so tests stub every engine (text, vision, embed, speak, listen) the same way.

## Description
types.ts promises that a provider is a swap and the caller's schema never changes. It is not true today: a non-isolated Claude call is schema-enforced, an isolated Claude call is not (text.ts:39-41), codex always is (codex.ts:40), and Ollama vision is decoder-enforced but falls back to a raw string on parse failure (vision.ts:28). All three providers then cast an unparseable answer to T (text.ts:63, codex.ts:58, vision.ts:28). The result is that five callers hand-guard their fields, four do not (pick.ts:19 throws a TypeError, analyse route crashes on a missing summary), and Linga re-implements its schema limits by hand in two files with the same five helpers copied (check.ts:21-26, conversation.ts:13-17). A shape verdict certified at LT on codex (AG-5) does not hold on the Claude engine the desk ships with. Tests reach the engines by reassigning CJS exports; embed/speak/listen cannot be stubbed, and retrieval cannot be tested at all because lessons.ts ignores DESK_DATA_DIR.

The move: engines/shape.ts - a validator for exactly the JSON-schema subset the tree uses (type object/string/integer/number/boolean/array, properties, required, additionalProperties:false, enum, minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, items; counted by grep: 72 type, 15 properties, 15 required, 21 items, 13 enum, 5 maxLength, 4 maxItems, 2 minItems, 1 minLength, 2 additionalProperties) plus the shared object/str/schema helpers; engines/registry.ts - useProvider(kind, impl), resetProviders(), activeProvider(kind), with claude-cli/codex/ollama/elevenlabs/piper/gravitone as registered defaults and DESK_TEXT_ENGINE choosing among them. text() and vision() become: provider returns raw -> strip fence once -> parse -> validate against req.schema -> EngineResult, or EngineError {kind: shape|timeout|exit|unreachable, provider, path}. pick.ts relies on the guarantee; lessons.ts honours DESK_DATA_DIR; check.ts/conversation.ts import the helpers instead of redefining them (their hand checks stay as the second, screen-fitting line).

## Flow
- caller: text({system, prompt, schema, model, isolated})
- registry picks the text provider (claude-cli by default, codex when DESK_TEXT_ENGINE=codex, a stub in tests)
- provider returns {raw, provider}
- engine: fence strip -> JSON.parse -> validate(schema) -> {json, provider, ms} or throw EngineError('shape', path)
- routes already catch and put a status line; Linga's call() already turns a throw into its error line

## Expected impact
A whole class of defect closes: a malformed model answer can no longer reach a caller typed as its shape (4 unguarded callers, 2 TypeError crash sites). The Claude and codex engines give the same shape guarantee, narrowing AG-5 without changing which engine ships. Every engine becomes stubbable through one seam, and retrieval becomes testable without touching desk/data. Decisions do not move: the validator checks shape only.

## Evaluation
Claim: the caller's schema is enforced identically for every provider, malformed answers fail as typed EngineErrors, and every engine and retrieval path can be stubbed under DESK_DATA_DIR.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 8 is a GUARD, green before); 3 string-as-T fallbacks, 2 fence-strip copies, 5 helpers duplicated across 2 files, 3 of 5 engines unstubbable except by export patching, 0 of 5 via a registry
After: 7 of 7 (and the GUARD green); 0 string-as-T fallbacks, 1 fence rule, 1 helper module
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/engines-rules-test.cjs (desk TS loader copied from tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:1-9), appended at the end of test:rules
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.body:
## Summary
Engine work (read a page, hint + lesson pick, write a practice set) becomes a job on the one session: {id, kind, state running|failed, line, input}. Results land only while their job is still current; a failure leaves a fixed human line and one Retry press on the phone that re-runs the job with what the desk already holds; the TV shows the job state in the caption slot instead of a wait that never ends.

## Description
Today the only trace of engine work is the free-text status (store.ts:79). Counted from the tree: 4 waits that never end on failure (hint status line, 'Finding the lesson…', the Page screen's 'reading' label, the Topics prep ticker on the TV), 3 late results that land on a desk that has moved on (hint stage-2 snapshot overwrite, lesson pick for a previous item, practice set for a previous learner), 5 routes that print raw engine error text, and 1 orphan empty page per failed read that also misnames the next page. The user's job is 'get past this problem tonight'; after any engine hiccup they are left guessing whether the desk is still working, and must re-snap, re-ask or back out and re-enter. Linga already solved this for itself (check.ts call(): pending token, result lands only on the same check, fixed failure line). This card gives the rest of the desk the same guarantee through the session, where both the TV and the phone see it.

jobs.ts: runJob(kind, key, input, work) sets s.job running, awaits work, applies the result only if s.job.id is still this job and the learner is unchanged, otherwise drops it; on throw sets state failed with a fixed per-kind line. work.ts: startRead/startHint/startPractice (the route bodies moved here, callable from tests) and retry(), which re-runs the failed job from its held input (read: the page image and id already on the session; hint: item key + askedQ; practice: topic). Routes become thin. Session POST refuses job.* events (403, as linga.changed). On Air: the TV shows the state as the caption (red chip label + one line), never asks for typing, puts nothing of the answer on screen; Retry lives on the phone (and Enter on the focused action where the screen already has one).

## Flow
- phone: Use this page -> POST /api/read -> startRead -> job running -> TV caption 'Reading the page'
- vision fails -> job failed 'The desk could not read that page.' -> page marked failed (no orphan, no endless 'reading')
- phone shows the line and one Retry button -> POST /api/session/retry -> same page id re-read -> job cleared, items on the TV
- learner moves to another item while the lesson pick runs -> the late pick is dropped

## Expected impact
Recovering from an engine failure goes from re-snap (open camera, frame, shoot, Use this page: 4 steps, plus a stray empty page on the TV) or back-out-and-re-enter to one press; no screen ever waits forever; a result is never shown against the wrong item or learner. Contract consumers of the new optional Session.job field and job events: tv/useSession.ts, app/tv/page.tsx, tv/screens.tsx, app/phone/page.tsx, english/LingaTV.tsx, english/LingaPhone.tsx, english/LingaTestBar.tsx, english/useEnglish.ts, app/english/print/page.tsx, app/api/session/route.ts, tools/linga-rules-test.cjs (reads getSession); only the first four read it, the rest compile unchanged. The TV change needs the overlay's Playwright capture on a second dev server with a seeded DESK_DATA_DIR.

## Evaluation
Claim: engine work on the session can no longer leave a screen waiting forever, land on a desk that moved on, or require re-capture to retry.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 8 is a GUARD, green before); 4 endless waits, 3 late-overwrite paths, 5 raw-error status sites, 1 orphan page per failed read
After: 7 of 7 (GUARD green); 0 / 0 / 0 / 0
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/session-rules-test.cjs (loader from tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:1-9, engines stubbed, scratch learner ids, DESK_DATA_DIR under OS tmp), plus the TV capture the overlay requires
Result: better
Gate: contract
